stem: A two-week randomised test of a redesigned homepage shows a significant 5% relative lift in clicks. A manager concludes: "So the redesign will give +5% relative for the next year." What is wrong with this conclusion?

options.text: Nothing: random assignment makes the measured lift hold for any period after the test
The lift is not causal, because a randomised test only shows a correlation with clicks
The test measured two weeks; the effect may fade, so the long run needs a longer look
The yearly effect is 26 times larger, because a year has 26 two-week periods of +5%
